title: The Warehouse Haven
story:
As the afternoon sun dipped low behind the riverbanks of San Antonio del Río, the frantic roar of the docks began to fade into a steady, rhythmic lapping of water against timber pilings. The cooling air brought a damp river mist that made the open wharves feel far too exposed for a quiet night's rest. Remembering how vulnerable they had been out in the open during past storms, James nudged Nico toward the long, low-slung silhouettes of the riverside warehouses lining the back of the quay.

Slip-sliding past a loading bay where dockworkers were battening down heavy wooden doors, James and his small companion squeezed through a loose slat in the side of a cavernous storage shed. Inside, the air was thick with the rich, earthy aromas of cured tobacco leaves and stacked jute sacks. It was dim, quiet, and wonderfully sheltered from the biting evening drafts sweeping off the water.

Trotting ahead with his large ears perked, Nico darted up a sturdy stack of empty crates toward the shadowed upper rafters where rolls of heavy canvas tarps were neatly benched. James followed agilely behind, exploring the high timber ledges until he discovered a deep, secluded alcove tucked completely out of sight behind a thick canvas roll.

James settled into the cozy nook with Nico behind the heavy canvas tarp, a warm, dry storage space entirely hidden from the dockhands below. Unfurling his weathered leather strap and pulling his pocket compass close, he felt a wave of quiet satisfaction wash over him as the distant hum of the river town lulled them toward sleep.
location: Riverside docks of San Antonio del Río
